title: Atomic rollforward and MVP cuts for console insight cards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Jules Park
description: PRD-level decision and acceptance criteria to reduce scope for Console dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown so we can ship a reliable MVP within the next cycle. This ticket defines the atomic rollforward strategy: which UI tiles and telemetry are in-scope, which tracing features are deferred, and how cost token-attribution will be simplified. It captures rationale, trade-offs, and the minimal engineering surface required for a shippable experience that supports Ops and early enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Launch with 3 consolidated insight cards (Route Overview, Top 5 Models by Token Cost, Recent Errors) rather than the full 9-card layout; each card has drill-to-detail links to logs/alerts.
Tracing: Provide sampling-based request traces for slow requests (p95+) with searchable trace IDs; advanced span visualization deferred to next milestone.
Cost breakdown: Provide per-route and per-model token breakdowns with aggregated daily buckets and a simple attribution model (no per-token stack traces) for MVP.
Performance: On load, dashboard p90 render time <= 400ms for datasets up to 24 hours (as measured in staging using synthetic workload).
Reliability: Dashboard and cost endpoints must have error rate < 0.5% over a 72h canary with 99th percentile API latency < 600ms.
Rollout gating: Feature stays behind 'console-mini' feature flag with opt-in for existing beta accounts; enablement must be toggleable per org.
Observability: Instrumentation must emit event tags that map to cost buckets so Optimize can consume them; existing billing pipelines are not modified for MVP (read-only integration).
Docs & UX: A concise help panel explaining the simplified attribution model and a link to the roadmap explaining deferred items must be present in the UI.
tradeoffs: Defer rich trace span flamegraphs and full-span search to reduce backend storage and query complexity — tradeoff: reduced debugging fidelity for early customers.
Consolidate multiple small insight cards into three higher-value cards to reduce frontend complexity and card-to-card data joins; tradeoff: less granular surface but faster iteration.
Simplify cost attribution to aggregated buckets (route/model/day) to avoid expensive per-request joins; tradeoff: inability to attribute micro-level token costs immediately.
Keep rollout behind feature flag to limit exposure; tradeoff: delays broad feedback but reduces blast radius.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal alpha: Deploy behind feature flag to staging, run synthetic load tests and trace sampling validation (2 days).

Phase 1 - limited beta (week 1): Enable for 5 friendly customer orgs; monitor error rates, dashboard render p95, and cost delta against billing. Roll back if error rate > 1% sustained or latency SLO violated.
Phase 2 - expanded beta (week 2): Expand to 25 orgs; collect qualitative feedback from SEs/CS and log support tickets; evaluate telemetry retention costs.
Phase 3 - GA candidate: Remove opt-in and flip default for new orgs; provide rollforward/rollback playbook to SRE.

notes_for_engineering: Implement lightweight query endpoints that return aggregated buckets; ensure idempotent pagination for card data. Add feature-flag gate and a metric (console.mini.feature_enable) for monitoring adoption.
ux_guidelines: Use progressive disclosure: each card shows a 1-line summary and a single CTA to 'Inspect' which opens the detailed flyout. Keep visual density low and show the simplified attribution explanation inline.
open_questions: What retention window should we ship with for sampled traces (7d vs 14d)? Engineering leaning to 7d to limit cost.
Should billing compare-run be performed weekly or daily for the initial beta? Ops prefers daily to catch regressions early.
Do we expose an 'export raw traces' button for enterprise customers on request? Legal/CX needs to sign off on data export policy.
